_comment: HUMAN-WRITTEN SYMPTOM LINES — what the model is told after a failed attempt.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. The repair loop used to derive its message from the
TEST TITLE. A test title states the RULE, so the message stated the rule:
gate E08 was reported as 'full-turn sequences are distinct by RESULTING
BOARD', which is the requirement verbatim. Measured on run 1788099503, the
model failed E08 on attempt 1 and passed it on attempt 2 — it was told. A
gate answered by its own failure message measures attempt count, not
capability.
THE VOICES. Two people report after a failure, and which one owns a line
depends on what kind of fault it is. The tester is a player of the
finished game who has noticed something wrong: they describe WHAT THEY
SAW, and they do not know the function names, the requirement ids, or the
fix — a user, not a reviewer. The integration team is a customer wiring
software against the app, reporting in "they/their" terms what their API
reads, health checks, and automation could not find or got wrong.
THE TEST: could a reader who has never seen the spec derive the fix from
this sentence alone? If yes, it is too specific. Name the surface (the
board, the dice, the pip numbers, the computer's move) and the wrongness.
Never name the rule.
BAD  'a checker on the bar counts a full 25 pips'   — states the rule
GOOD 'my counter barely moved while my piece sat on the bar'
Each gate carries TWO lines, and which one is sent depends on whether this
is the first time the model is hearing about that gate or a repeat.
first   — the player's first report, after their first playthrough.
repeat  — the SAME fault, seen again on a replay, after the model has
already tried to fix it and failed.
WHY TWO AND NOT ONE. Byte-identical text across attempts returns ZERO new
information: a failed fix reads exactly like a fix never attempted, and the
repair loop has no gradient. That is the defect WO-FEEDBACK-1 fixed by
appending the grader's own assertion text on a repeat — which worked, and
leaked. The assertion states the rule, which is the one thing this file
exists to withhold. The second line replaces it.
WHAT A REPEAT LINE IS ALLOWED TO ADD. A SECOND SIGHTING, not a rephrase:
the player went back and played again, and reports the same fault from a
different observable angle — what they did differently, what they watched
for, what they compared it against. Confirmation that the fix missed is
itself real information and costs nothing. The anti-leak test above applies
to the repeat line UNCHANGED, and it is the harder line to write: a second
description drifts toward the cause if it is not held back deliberately.
THIRD AND LATER FAILURES REUSE THE REPEAT LINE. A person does not invent
fresh phrasing every round, and a third variant would either repeat itself
or start narrowing toward the fix.
PROVISIONAL — RE-GAUGE AFTER SEVERAL CAMPAIGNS (2026-09-02). These lines
have not been measured yet. Once several benchmarks have run, take the
gates that are ALWAYS failing and read the prose those gates feed the
model: a gate that never goes green may be under-specified rather than
hard, and the ambiguity would be here, not in the model. See
dev/priv/dev-bench-prompts.md.
